name: Bookokrat
summary: A terminal reader for EPUB, PDF and DJVU books with Vim-style keybindings, search, bookmarks and annotations.
use_cases: read an EPUB book in the terminal
view a PDF in the terminal
jump between LaTeX source and PDF output with SyncTeX
features: read EPUB, PDF and DJVU files
annotate with comments exported to Markdown

system_packages: pkg-config, libfontconfig1-dev, clang, libclang-dev (for PDF/DJVU on Debian/Ubuntu)

manual_steps: Use a graphics-capable terminal such as Kitty or Ghostty to view PDF and DJVU

pitfalls.readme_said: Install via cargo, AUR (yay/paru), Nix, or prebuilt Linux binaries from GitHub Releases
pitfalls.actually_needed: This box has no Rust, Arch or Nix, so I used the prebuilt release binary.

pitfalls.readme_said: Prebuilt Linux binaries: download from GitHub Releases
pitfalls.actually_needed: The x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu binary needs the system library libfontconfig.so.1 (package libfontconfig1). Without it, the binary fails to start with exit 127. The musl build starts without it.
The static musl build panics on PDFs with 'Dynamic loading not supported' (fontconfig dlopen). PDF needs the gnu build plus libfontconfig1, which this box cannot install without root.

judge.observed: All three checks exit 0 and print their expected signals: the book text with the fox sentence, a TOC listing Chapter One and Chapter Two, and the help text with the tagline.

features.feature: read EPUB, PDF and DJVU files
features.note: no failed check in the log; EPUB works: content and TOC printed. PDF failed: the musl build panics on a fontconfig dlopen, and the gnu build needs libfontconfig1, which can't be installed without root. DJVU not tried.
Search, bookmarks and stats only run inside the interactive TUI. My pty-driven attempt could not show that search actually worked.

features.feature: annotate with comments exported to Markdown
features.note: Comments and Markdown export only run inside the interactive TUI.
--print-default-keybindings-grouped lists Vim bindings (j/k/gg/G/dd), but I could not check that navigation actually works without an interactive terminal.
